items.prompt: Why are total trade lines O(n) even though selecting a best level can scan many prices?

options.text: Each match exhausts a resting L order or its current M order.
options.why: Charge the match to an event exhausted at that step; an exhausted event cannot fund another such charge.

options.text: Every event emits exactly one trade line.
options.why: A market event can emit multiple lines across different resting orders.

options.text: All same-price orders are merged before execution.
options.why: The source preserves their individual FIFO boundaries.

options.text: The best-price scan is worst-case constant time.
options.why: It can scan O(n) levels; that affects total time, not the linear bound on match lines.

items.explanation: Charge the match to an event exhausted at that step; an exhausted event cannot fund another such charge.
